units.text: In other locales, the sorting sequence is not specified, and ‘⟦0⟧’ might be equivalent to ‘⟦1⟧’ or to ‘⟦2⟧’, or it might fail to match any character, or the set of characters that it matches might even be erratic. To obtain the traditional interpretation of bracket expressions, you can use the ‘⟦3⟧’ locale by setting the ⟦4⟧ environment variable to the value ‘⟦5⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: In other locales, the sorting sequence is not specified, and ‘[a-d]’ might be equivalent to ‘[abcd]’ or to ‘[aBbCcDd]’, or it might fail to match any character, or the set of characters that it matches might even be erratic. To obtain the traditional interpretation of bracket expressions, you can use the ‘C’ locale by setting the LC_ALL environment variable to the value ‘C’.

units.text: Their interpretation depends on the ⟦0⟧ locale; for example, ‘⟦1⟧’ means the character class of numbers and letters in the current locale.
units.sourceHTML: Their interpretation depends on the LC_CTYPE locale; for example, ‘[[:alnum:]]’ means the character class of numbers and letters in the current locale.
